claims.statement: The OAuth Server-to-Server credential generates access tokens with the OAuth 2.0 client_credentials grant, using the credential's client_id and client_secret (with scopes) in a token request; the client_secret must be used only on a secure backend server.

sources.supports: OAuth Server-to-Server credential relies on the client_credentials grant; a single HTTP request with client_id, client_secret and scopes generates a token; the logic must run on a secure backend server to prevent malicious actors from accessing secrets.

Fetching access tokens: client_id (mandatory, the Client ID from the Developer Console) and client_secret (mandatory, the value of client secret obtained from the Developer Console) are request parameters.

claims.statement: A credential can hold up to 2 client secrets; secrets can be added, listed (the list returns only a uuid and metadata, never the secret value) and deleted through the Developer Console UI or the I/O Management API; the add response returns the new client_secret once, and it is otherwise visible only in the Developer Console UI.

sources.supports: You can add up to 2 client secrets; no client_secret values are returned by the list API; the add response contains the client_secret, which will never be returned in plain text by any other API response.
sources.locator: sections "List all client secrets" and "Add client secret to credential"

sources.supports: Secrets can be rotated through the Dev Console UI and programmatically; a deleted client secret cannot be restored.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: Adobe documentation read for this candidate gives no prefix, alphabet, length or other format rule for this value; any example in it is a placeholder or a public identifier. Not researched beyond existence.

The documentation shows an example client_id but no rule for it, and no example client_secret value (placeholder only). Whether the client ID and the client secret are distinguishable by shape is not established; the client ID is a public identifier (sent as the x-api-key header) and must not be treated as the secret.
